subject: Residency operations: request for temporary egress windows & audit playbook
messages:
From: Alice Meng <alice.meng@biosync.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.example.com>
Cc: DPO Team <dpo@biosync.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 09:15:00 +0000
Subject: Residency question: short transient egress window for vendor scans

Karthik —

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. A couple of follow-ups from our security team: we run quarterly external vulnerability scans that occasionally require copies of logs (sanitized) to be pulled for third-party scanning tools that are EU-hosted but operate a short processing window in the US for enrichment.

Two asks: can Redwood commit to a documented operational window (e.g., max 72 hours) for any transient cross-border processing tied to these scans, and can we get an auditable trail that shows which records were exported and when?

If you already have a standard playbook, could you share it (even draft)? Otherwise, can your team propose how you’d limit scope and retention for scan artifacts?

Appreciate it,
Alice Meng
Head of Security Operations
BioSync Therapeutics

Attachment: scan-scope-template.xlsx (attachment referenced)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.example.com>
To: Alice Meng <alice.meng@biosync.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.example.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 12:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Residency question: short transient egress window for vendor scans

Alice —

Short answer: yes, we can support a limited transient processing window and provide audit logs that record exports and who triggered them. I want to surface a few implementation trade-offs so expectations line up: 

- Scope: we can restrict exported artifacts to a named log index or a specific bucket and a timestamp range. That scope must be pre-authorized per-submission to avoid ad-hoc broad exports.
- Retention: we can set a hard TTL on exported artifacts (recommended 24–72 hours) after which objects are irreversibly deleted.
- Auditability: exports generate an immutable event (who, what, when, route) in our audit logs; we can also include a SHA256 manifest of exported files for verification by your auditor.

Laura and Marissa — can you pull a draft playbook? I’m thinking: request intake, authorization (DPO OK), narrow-scope export job, ephemeral storage in an EU-only bucket with lifecycle delete, and an audit manifest sent to the customer. I’ve attached a short checklist to start.

Karthik
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: residency-egress-playbook-v1.pdf (first draft checklist)

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.example.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.example.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Alice Meng <alice.meng@biosync.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 08:22:00 +0000
Subject: Proposed playbook and retention defaults

Team / Alice —

I’m attaching a concise operational playbook (PDF) and a proposed default policy:

- Authorization: DPO sign-off via email or DocuSign token before job creation.
- Export scope: named indices / buckets only; no free-form SQL exports.
- TTL: default 48 hours; customer can request up to 72 hours with justification.
- Access: exported artifacts stored in an EU-only ephemeral bucket; only a single pre-authorized external IP range allowed for scanner retrieval.
- Audit: event emitted to both Redwood and customer audit streams; manifest includes SHA256 and object sizes.

Alice — if that aligns, we’ll add the specific request intake fields you shared and prep a DPA addendum with the TTL language for signatures.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachment: residency-egress-playbook-v1.pdf

From: DPO Team <dpo@biosync.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.example.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.example.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 09:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Proposed playbook and retention defaults

Laura / Karthik —

This looks promising and addresses the majority of concerns. A few clarifications before we sign off:

1) Evidence: can Redwood provide sample audit entries (anonymized) so our auditor can validate the manifest fields?
2) Subprocessor disclosure: will any part of the export pipeline (e.g., storage, transfer) be handed to a third party in a non-EU jurisdiction? We need confirmation of the roster for the specific export flow.
3) Emergency access: in the rare case of legal hold, what is your escalation path and how quickly can you pause TTL deletion?

We’d like a short phrase in the DPA addendum that describes the max transient processing window and the requirement for a signed intake per export.

Best,
BioSync DPO Team

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.example.com>
To: DPO Team <dpo@biosync.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.example.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example.com>, grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.example.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2026 16:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Proposed playbook and retention defaults — answers and next steps

DPO Team / Alice —

Thanks — answers inline: 

1) Sample audit entries: yes, we’ll generate a 3-line anonymized sample that shows timestamp, initiating identity (customer token), export manifest (filenames + SHA256), and deletion lifecycle events. We’ll include it in the DPA addendum appendix.

2) Subprocessors: the export path uses our EU object storage provider (Redwood-managed) and a short transfer service that is under contract with Redwood. If the transfer service needs to transiently route via a US staging node for enrichment, we will call that out explicitly in the export request and require customer authorization; otherwise the default flow remains EU-only. We’ll provide the transfer subprocessor roster and SOC evidence in the addendum.

3) Emergency/legal hold: we can pause TTL deletion within 2 hours of a validated legal hold request submitted by your legal or DPO email; we’ll also emit an immediate audit event when hold is placed. That pause is limited to the specific export job unless otherwise requested via formal process.

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa to draft DPA addendum language that includes the transient window (default 48h, max 72h), sample audit entry, and subprocessors roster.
- Grace to produce anonymized sample audit entries and a sample manifest.
- We’ll circulate a DocuSign addendum for signature; once countersigned we’ll enable the intake flow.

Tom Ruiz (cc’d) from procurement — can you confirm if BioSync wants the addendum integrated into the master SOW or as a separate annex for faster execution?

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: dpa-addendum-proposed-redlines.docx
